root_cause.text: The `__tb_property_parse_dir()` function lacks a bounds check for the root directory case, allowing a crafted property block where the root directory’s declared length causes `content_offset + content_len` to exceed `block_len`, leading to an out-of-bounds read in the entry loop.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: “__tb_property_parse_dir() does not check that content_offset + content_len fits within block_len for the root directory case. When rootdir->length equals or exceeds block_len - 2, the entry loop reads past the allocated property block.” The patch adds the missing check: `if (content_offset + content_len > block_len) { ... return NULL; }`.

bic_trace_step.reason: In __tb_property_parse_dir, for the root directory case (is_root=true), the code sets content_offset = dir_offset + 2 (i.e., 2 dwords past the start) and content_len = dir_len. Then entries = &block[content_offset] and nentries = content_len / 4. There is no check that content_offset + content_len <= block_len, so a crafted root directory with a large dir_len can cause the loop to read past the end of the block. The caller tb_property_parse_dir only checks rootdir->length > block_len but not the combined offset+length. This matches the root cause: missing bounds check for root directory case.
